name: Trickplayer
description: Watch an episode on your Even Realities G2 as trick-play frames and subtitles: the picture updates every few seconds while the dialogue keeps pace, so you follow the story without a screen in front of you. Connects to your own Plex server.

permissions.name: network
permissions.desc: Connects to plex.tv to sign in, and to your own Plex server to download trick-play frames and subtitles. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

notes: The display no longer blanks and redraws every 15 seconds during playback. The recent list's labels carry a resume time that ticks along with playback, and updating them was rebuilding the whole glasses page.
Resuming after a pause no longer drops the picture quality. The first frame after resuming waits behind another send, and that wait was being counted as a slow link.
Choosing something from the recent list while a video is playing now stops the first one instead of playing both at once.
A menu on the glasses (tap, then long press): Play / Pause, Stop — which returns to the recent list — and Recently played.
Using the menu no longer pauses playback. The menu overlay hands the foreground back as it closes, which the app had been treating as the phone leaving the app.
Starting a video from the phone now clears the recent list off the glasses — it was covering the picture while subtitles showed underneath it.
Picking from the recent list starts the item you can see. Playing something reorders the list, and the picker was left showing the old order, so a tap started the wrong video.
"Select video to begin" no longer appears under the picture during quiet stretches.
Picture quality recovers on a merely slow link. It only climbed back after unusually fast sends, so a moderately slow link left the picture coarse for the rest of the session.
The app returns to the smaller picture format once frames are landing again, instead of sending double-size ones for the rest of the session.

Playback resumes where you stopped. Position is remembered while you watch, and picking an item — from the glasses list or the phone — carries on from there. Items you nearly finished start again from the beginning.
The glasses say "Loading [title]" as soon as you pick something, instead of leaving "Select video to begin" up while the index loads.
A stretch with no subtitles now clears the line instead of leaving the previous scene's dialogue under an unrelated picture.
The glasses now show a frame where the picture will be and "Select video to begin" when nothing is playing, instead of "Sign in to Plex".
Your last five played items are remembered. They appear as a list on the glasses at startup — scroll with the temple, tap to start — so you can resume without touching the phone.
A "Recently played" entry in the glasses menu brings that list back during playback.
Browsing into an episode and back no longer re-checks every episode in the list; answers are kept for the session.
Logging reports no longer claim playback stopped for no reason when you were only browsing, and no longer record an "end of playback" or "left the item" while nothing is playing.
A tap on the glasses pauses playback — it now says "Paused - tap to resume" on the glasses instead of just stopping, which looked identical to a freeze.

Everything that can stop playback is now recorded: taps on the glasses, double-taps, exits, leaving the item, and the end of an episode. A session stopped mid-episode and nothing in the report could say what did it.
Logging reports now call out playback stopping with nothing to explain it, instead of writing it off as browsing.
A fourth, smallest picture level for when the link slows badly: very coarse, but about a third the size of the previous smallest, so it has a much better chance of getting through.

Pictures are no longer paused for up to a minute while smaller ones are still getting through. Pausing now only happens once even the smallest pictures keep failing, and never for more than 20 seconds.
The app no longer rebuilds the glasses display when pictures are merely slow — that only helps when the glasses refuse a picture outright.
Logging reports show subtitle send times per minute alongside pictures, which tells a slow link apart from a picture problem.

Running a picture sweep from the logging panel no longer sets off the app's picture recovery. The sweep sends sizes chosen to fail, and those failures were making the app rebuild the glasses display mid-test and pause pictures — and playback then started already in that state.
The locked sweep now pauses between test pictures instead of sending them back to back.

Logging reports no longer count a sweep's failures as the picture stopping, no longer judge lighter pictures from a single frame, and say when a session was cut off rather than calling it 'not a disconnect'.
Logging reports now show picture sends minute by minute, marking any slow or failing minute and which picture level was used — so a slowdown is visible even though the app can't see the phone lock.
Two report findings no longer claim things the session's own data contradicts.

Pictures now keep coming with the phone locked. Locking the phone slows the Bluetooth link, and full-size pictures stopped finishing in time — subtitles, being tiny, still did. When sending gets slow or fails, the app now switches to lighter pictures (4 shades, then half resolution as well) that get through, and returns to full pictures once the link is fast again.
Logging reports show results for each picture level and every switch between them.

New in the logging build: "Sweep with the phone LOCKED". Start it, lock the phone, and it tests picture sizes on its own — to find out whether the glasses stop taking pictures when the phone is locked, or only the larger ones stop getting through.
Logging reports now say when the app itself kept running normally while pictures failed.
Logging reports now show whether failures happen while the phone is asleep — measured from how late the app's own timers run, since the phone never tells the app it has gone to sleep.

Reports now list every pause and resume for the whole session, including when the glasses app says it lost the foreground and when you press play, and whether the background keep-alive was actually running.
Reports no longer blame the headset: the glasses can report "not worn" while you are wearing them.

When the glasses keep refusing pictures, the app now pauses sending them for a little while — 10 seconds, growing to a minute — and tries again, instead of sending another every few seconds. Subtitles carry on throughout.
Logging reports now show how long failed picture sends take, whether failures happened with the glasses on or off your head, and what the app was waiting on during any silence.

Your Plex server now loads away from home. The app used to pick one of the server's addresses when you signed in — at home, the home-network one — and use it forever, so on mobile data or another Wi-Fi it could only work over a VPN. It now tries every address Plex lists at once, uses the best one that answers, and switches automatically when you change networks, even mid-episode.
If the server really can't be reached from where you are, it says why — including when Plex only lists a home-network address, which usually means Remote Access is off in the server's settings.

When the picture stops but subtitles keep coming, the app now actually recovers. Every earlier repair used a setup call the glasses only accept at launch, so it was refused every time and changed nothing. It now rebuilds the page the supported way.

The app no longer switches to a slower picture format when frames fail after the current one has already been working — and no longer remembers that switch, which could have left the picture on the slowest path for good.
Logging reports now put a picture that died for good at the top, measure how long it was frozen, and say what recovery was tried.

The picture should appear again. Your glasses accepted every synthetic payload the sweep sent and refused every real frame, and the only difference was how the frame was encoded. The app now tries a second and a third encoding when frames keep failing, and remembers whichever one works.
New "Which image formats work?" button: sends one picture encoded three ways and reports which the glasses accept. Twenty seconds, and it settles the question outright.
The sweep now refuses to run during playback. It is a minute of writes on a serial link, and started mid-episode it queues in front of everything — which is why subtitles took a minute to appear.
The report no longer leads with advice about payload size when the real problem is that none of the app's own frames are landing.

The logging session survives a relaunch. It was being written to browser storage, which a packaged app discards — the same thing that used to lose your server — so a crash took the recording of the crash with it.
Logging stays on across relaunches once you turn it on, and starts recording before the app does anything, so the launch itself is inside the session. A new "Stop logging" button turns it off.
A session that recorded a freeze is no longer thrown away. An outage is an absence of writes, and the resume rule only kept sessions that had writes in them.

"Connect with logging" no longer ends the app. It used to open a second page, and on the glasses opening a page is a navigation — the G2 offers to end the feature, the display containers go with it, and the picture never comes back. The recorder now switches on where you are, without going anywhere.
Discard session did the same thing for the same reason, and no longer does.
When an image write is refused, the report now says what the glasses actually answered instead of only how many failed.
Your server is remembered again. A packaged app does not keep its own browser storage, so sign-in is now held by the host — it survives a relaunch.

The picture no longer freezes in silence when the server becomes unreachable. Frames come off the network every few seconds while subtitles are held in memory, so losing the server used to stop the picture and leave the dialogue running with no explanation. It now says so, and recovers on its own.
A dropped link could kill either the picture or the subtitles and leave the other running. Recovery now works in both directions; it previously only handled one.
"Connect with logging" on the first screen opens the build that records the link and writes a report.
First beta.
Plex sign-in by four-character code — no keyboard, no password on the glasses.
Continuous playback: frames advance on the measured link speed rather than a fixed timer.

Rebuilt Bluetooth transport — newest frame wins a backlog, a failed line is re-sent instead of being remembered as delivered, and a dropped link no longer leaves the subtitles dead for the rest of the session.
Frames are prepared about 50x faster, which was four seconds a frame on some phones.
